# **Introduction** {#introduction}

1. ## ***Purpose*** {#purpose}

This Software Design Document (SDD) describes the architectural and detailed design of AlkaSense, a mobile application currently developed for Android that automates the Alkali Spreading Value (ASV) scoring process for rice gelatinisation temperature classification at the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice). The SDD translates the functional and non-functional requirements specified in the AlkaSense Software Requirements Specification (SRS v2.0, May 16, 2026\) into concrete design decisions covering system architecture, module decomposition, data design, and interface specifications.

This document is intended for use by the AlkaSense development team as the primary technical reference during implementation, integration, and testing. It also serves as a baseline for design reviews by project supervisors and PhilRice stakeholders. Where requirements in the SRS are refined or decomposed into design-level decisions, this document is the authoritative source.

2. ## ***Scope*** {#scope}

This SDD covers the complete design of the AlkaSense system as scoped in SRS v2.0. The system consists of:

* A **React Native / Expo Android client application** providing five integrated functional modules: Evaluation Session and Sample Registration, Image Submission and Quality Validation, Expert Evaluation Recording and AI-Assisted Scoring, Session Reporting and Institutional Data Submission, and Scoring Reference Library access.  
* An **on-device data layer** implemented via Expo SQLite, persisting all evaluation data offline-first.  
* A **FastAPI backend** hosted on Render, handling Grad-CAM explainability computation, session report upload, and administrator report retrieval, backed by a PostgreSQL database.  
* A **TensorFlow Lite inference engine** executing an EfficientNet-B1 CNN model on-device for ASV classification.  
* **Firebase Authentication** for identity management and role-based access control.

The design covers all four modules and their constituent transactions as defined in the SRS. iOS deployment, a dedicated web evaluator interface, and model retraining pipelines are explicitly out of scope.

1. # **Architectural Design** {#architectural-design}

1. **Client-side Architecture: Android Device Components**

*![][image1]*

The Android device layer constitutes the entirety of the core evaluation workflow. All session management, sample registration, image capture, on-device CNN inference, observation entry, score confirmation, correction logging, and local data persistence operate without requiring an active network connection, fulfilling the offline-first requirement. The TFLite CNN model is bundled within the application package at build time and its SHA-256 hash is verified via expo-crypto at every application startup before inference is permitted. The observation-score conflict logic is a custom rule table — not a third-party library — that maps each predicted ASV score against expected ranges for all five evaluator observation dimensions to detect inconsistencies. Correction log records written to expo-sqlite are stored independently of the original ConfirmedScore records and do not overwrite them, preserving the full audit trail. 

Heatmap PNG files returned by the FastAPI backend are cached to expo-file-system and displayed from cache when the device is offline, ensuring the explainability feature degrades gracefully without blocking the evaluation session. The model training environment shown has no runtime connection to the deployed system and is represented solely to illustrate the origin of the bundled TFLite binary. PDF batch reports are generated within 10 seconds of session closure and CSV exports within 5 seconds of the evaluator's request, as required by the performance non-functional requirements. 

2. **Server-side Architecture: Backend, External Services, and Admin Interface** 

*![][image2]*

Firebase Authentication serves exclusively as the identity provider for AlkaSense. It issues signed JSON Web Tokens upon successful login, which are attached as Bearer credentials to all outbound API requests from the mobile client to the FastAPI backend. No application data — sessions, evaluation records, corrections, or reports — is stored in Firebase; all server-side persistence is handled exclusively by PostgreSQL through the FastAPI application layer. Grad-CAM heatmap computation is executed server-side because it requires access to the full Keras model graph, which is not available in the TFLite runtime deployed on-device. LIME explainability is an optional server-side function used for batch report context only and is not surfaced inline on the mobile evaluation screen. 

The PostgreSQL database stores uploaded session report packages accessible to PhilRice administrators and has no direct connection to the mobile client — all reads and writes are mediated through FastAPI. The Jinja2 administrator interface is a minimal server-rendered web interface for report retrieval and is intended as an interim solution; a dedicated web application for PhilRice administrators is identified as a planned future extension beyond the current project scope. Failed report uploads are retried using exponential backoff, with an initial delay of 2 seconds doubling up to a ceiling of 60 seconds, and the report package is retained in local device storage until a server-confirmed receipt is received. All communication between the mobile client and the FastAPI backend is conducted over HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher enforced, and certificate pinning is implemented client-side to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks.

### ***Module 1: Evaluation Session and Sample Registration System*** {#module-1:-evaluation-session-and-sample-registration-system}

#### ***1.1: Session Creation***

* User Interface Design

![][image3]

* Front-end component(s)

| Component Name | Description & Purpose | Type / Format |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Session Name Input Field | Accepts a user-defined label for the evaluation session such as a variety trial name or date-based identifier; enforces a non-empty, non-duplicate value before the session can be created | Single-line text input field |
| Batch Identifier Input Field | Captures the batch code associated with the entire group of samples being evaluated in this session; all subsequent sample records inherit this identifier automatically | Single-line text input field |
| KOH Concentration Input Field | Captures the potassium hydroxide solution concentration in percentage units that applies uniformly to every sample in this session; entered once at session level to eliminate per-sample re-entry | Numeric input field with unit label |
| Incubation Duration Input Field | Captures the total alkali incubation time in hours that applies uniformly across all samples registered under this session | Numeric input field with unit labe |
| Evaluation Date Field | Records the date on which the evaluation session is being conducted; auto-populated with the current device date but editable by the evaluator if backdating is required | Date picker field |
| Evaluator Identity Display | Shows the currently logged-in evaluator's name and role automatically drawn from the active user record; non-editable and always visible during session creation | Read-only display label |
| Session Start Button | Triggers session record creation with all entered batch-level metadata and navigates the evaluator to the Sample Registration screen; disabled until all mandatory fields carry valid values | Primary action button |
| Validation Error Banner | Displays inline feedback when mandatory fields are empty, numeric values are out of acceptable range, or a duplicate session name is detected; prevents submission until all errors are resolved | Inline error message component |

| Protocol Compliance Checklist Panel | Presents a pre-submission checklist requiring the evaluator to confirm correct physical capture conditions before the Submit Image Button becomes active; checklist items cover UV or blacklight illumination confirmed, white tray background in use, grains arranged in a single layer, and petri dish fully within the frame; all items must be checked before submission is permitted | Multi-item checkbox panel with submission gate logic |

| Gallery Upload Button | Opens the device image gallery and allows the evaluator to select a previously captured image for submission in place of a live camera capture | Secondary action button with gallery intent |
| Image Preview | Displays a thumbnail or directs to the captured or selected image before submission so the evaluator can visually confirm the framing and lighting before sending for validation | Image preview component |
| Submit Image Button | Sends the selected or captured image and the completed checklist confirmation to the quality validation pipeline linked to the current sample record; disabled until both an image is present in the preview panel and all checklist items are confirmed | Primary action button |
| Retake or Reselect Button | Clears the current image from the preview panel and returns the evaluator to the capture or gallery selection state without submitting anything | Secondary action button |

#### ***2.2: Image Validation and Resubmission***

* User Interface Design

![][image21]

* Front-end component(s)

| Component Name | Description & Purpose | Type / Format |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Validation Status Banner | Displays the outcome of the two-layer validation — Accepted, Protocol Violation, or Quality Failure — prominently at the top of the screen immediately after validation completes; uses distinct color states for each outcome | Status banner component with three conditional color states |
| Layer-Identified Rejection Reason Display | When the image is rejected, displays the specific layer — Protocol Violation or Quality Failure — alongside a plain-language description of the exact condition that failed, so the evaluator knows precisely what to correct before resubmitting | Conditional text display component, visible only on rejection |
| Protocol Correction Guidance Panel | When rejection is due to a protocol violation, displays specific corrective instructions corresponding to the failed checklist item — for example, ensure UV illumination is active before recapturing — to guide the evaluator's physical correction | Conditional guidance panel, visible only on protocol rejection |
| Accepted Image Confirmation Panel | When the image passes both validation layers, displays the validated image thumbnail alongside a confirmation message and enables navigation to Module 3 | When the image passes both validation layers, displays the validated image thumbnail alongside a confirmation message and enables navigation to Module 3 |
| Resubmit Image Button | Returns the evaluator to the Image Submission Screen for the same sample so a corrected image and updated checklist can be submitted; only visible on rejection | Secondary action button, conditionally rendered |
| Proceed to Evaluation Button | Navigates the evaluator to the Expert Observation Entry screen for this sample; only active and visible when the image has passed both validation layers | Primary action button, conditionally rendered |

| :---- | :---- |

### ***Module 3: Expert Evaluation Recording and AI-Assisted Scoring System*** {#module-3:-expert-evaluation-recording-and-ai-assisted-scoring-system}

#### ***3.1: Expert Observation Entry***

* User Interface Design

* Front-end component(s)

| Component Name | Description & Purpose | Type / Format |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Sample and Image Context Banner | Displays the sample identifier, rice variety, grain count, session name, and a thumbnail of the validated grain image so the evaluator has full context while completing the observation form | Read-only header with image thumbnail component |
| Spreading Pattern Texture Selector | Presents categorical options for the evaluator to classify the observed spreading pattern of the grain — Smooth and Continuous, Ragged and Fragmented, Partial Spreading Only, or No Spreading — based on direct visual inspection of the petri dish | Single-select option group |
| Grain Translucency Selector | Presents categorical options for the evaluator to classify the degree of translucency observed in the grain body — Fully Translucent, Partially Translucent, or Opaque — reflecting the gelatinization state independent of spread extent | Single-select option group |
| Within-Dish Score Uniformity Selector | Presents categorical options for the evaluator to classify how consistent the spreading behavior was across all grains in the petri dish — Uniform, Moderate Variation, or High Variation — which informs confidence in the sample-level score | Single-select option group |
| Anomaly Flag Selector | Presents categorical options for the evaluator to flag any anomalous grain behavior observed — Longitudinal Cracking, Unilateral Spreading, Floating Grains, No Anomaly — with multi-select enabled since multiple anomaly types may occur simultaneously | Multi-select option group |
| KOH Solution Appearance Selector | Presents categorical options for the evaluator to record the post-incubation appearance of the KOH solution in the dish — Clear, Mildly Clouded, or Heavily Clouded — which can indicate contamination or over-dissolution conditions | Single-select option group |
| Save and Request AI Draft Button | Saves the completed observation profile to the evaluation record and navigates the evaluator to Transaction 3.2 to optionally invoke AI scoring; disabled until all five observation dimensions carry a selection | Primary action button |
| Save and Score Manually Button | Saves the completed observation profile and navigates the evaluator directly to Transaction 3.3 for manual score entry without AI involvement; the observation profile alone constitutes a complete and storable evaluation input | Secondary action button |
| Validation Error Banner | Surfaces feedback when any of the five observation dimensions has not yet received a selection; prevents form submission until all dimensions are complete | Inline error message component |

#### ***3.2: AI-Assisted Draft Score Generation*** {#3.2:-ai-assisted-draft-score-generation}

* User Interface Design

![][image32]

* Front-end component(s)

| Component Name | Description & Purpose | Type / Format |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Sample Context and Observation Summary Panel | Displays the sample identifier, validated grain image thumbnail, and a collapsed read-only summary of the evaluator's five completed observation dimension selections so evaluation context is maintained while reviewing the AI draft | Read-only composite display component |
| Request AI Draft Button | Triggers the on-device AI classification for the current sample, passing both the validated grain image and the structured observation profile as joint inputs; only available after the observation form is complete | Primary action button |
| AI Draft Score Display | Renders the AI-generated ASV score on a color-coded 1–7 scale, the mapped gelatinization temperature class, and the gelatinization temperature range after classification completes | Composite result display component |
| Certainty Level Indicator | Displays the computed certainty percentage alongside the draft score, incorporating both the model's raw image confidence and any detected conflicts with the observation profile | Numeric and visual indicator component |
| Low-Certainty Warning Banner | Appears automatically when the model's raw classification confidence falls below the defined threshold; labeled distinctly as a Model Confidence Warning so the evaluator understands the uncertainty originates from the image classification | Conditional warning banner |
| Observation-Score Conflict Warning Banner | Appears automatically when the draft score is inconsistent with one or more of the evaluator's five observation dimension selections; labeled distinctly as an Observation Conflict Warning and identifies which specific observation dimension conflicts with the draft result | Conditional warning banner, separate from Low-Certainty Warning Banner |
| Visual Evidence Overlay Viewer | Displays the validated grain image with a heatmap overlay highlighting the regions of the grain that most influenced the AI draft score; rendered alongside the draft result for evaluator reference | Image display component with overlay rendering layer |
| Proceed to Confirm Score Button | Navigates the evaluator to the Score Confirmation screen carrying the AI draft score, certainty level, and any active warning flags as pre-loaded reference values; the evaluator is not committed to accepting the draft | Primary action button |

* Back-end component(s)

  * Component Name

    * Description and purpose

    * Component type or format

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | AIScoreRequestHandler |
| Description and Purpose | Receives the scoring request from the front end, retrieves the validated image file path and completed observation profile for the sample, and coordinates classification, conflict detection, overlay generation, and result storage |
| Component Type / Format | Service class / request handler |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | OnDeviceClassifier |
| Description and Purpose | Runs the validated grain image through the locally deployed classification model and returns a structured result containing the predicted ASV score, gelatinization temperature class, gelatinization temperature range, and raw confidence score |
| Component Type / Format | On-device inference service |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | ObservationConflictDetector |
| Description and Purpose | Compares the classifier's predicted ASV score against the evaluator's five structured observation dimension selections and returns a list of specific observation dimensions that are inconsistent with the predicted score, if any |
| Component Type / Format | Conflict analysis service |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | CertaintyComputor |
| Description and Purpose | Computes the final displayed certainty level by combining the model's raw confidence score with the conflict severity detected by ObservationConflictDetector; returns a calibrated certainty percentage and flags for low-certainty and conflict warning display |
| Component Type / Format | Utility service |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | EvidenceOverlayGenerator |
| Description and Purpose | Generates the visual evidence overlay image for the submitted grain image based on the classification result and saves the overlay file to local storage linked to the evaluation record |
| Component Type / Format | Image processing service |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | DraftScoreRepository |
| Description and Purpose | Writes the complete AI draft result — ASV score, GT class, GT range, certainty score, low-certainty flag, conflict flag, conflicting observation dimensions, and overlay file path — to the DraftScore table linked to the current evaluation record; updates EvaluationRecord status to draft\_generated |
| Component Type / Format | Repository class / data access object |

#### ***3.3: Evaluator Score Confirmation*** {#3.3:-evaluator-score-confirmation}

* User Interface Design

| Conflict Resolution Remark Field | A mandatory free-text field that appears specifically when an observation-score conflict warning was flagged in Transaction 3.2; prompts the evaluator to address and resolve the specific flagged conflict in writing; distinct from the general deviation remark | Conditional mandatory text input field, separate from Score Deviation Remark Field |
| Confirm Score Button | Submits the evaluator's final score selection along with all required remarks and writes the confirmed result to the ConfirmedScore table; disabled until all mandatory conditions are satisfied including remark fields where required | Primary action button |
| Confirmed Score Summary Display | After successful confirmation, replaces the input interface with a read-only summary showing the confirmed ASV score, GT classification, evaluator name, confirmation timestamp, AI draft used status, and whether a deviation or conflict resolution remark was recorded | Post-confirmation read-only summary component |

| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | ScoreCorrectionHandler |
| Description and Purpose | Receives the correction submission, validates that the corrected score differs from the original, that the remark field is populated, and that the submitting evaluator is certified; writes the correction record to the CorrectionLog table |
| Component Type / Format | Service class / request handler |

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Component Name | CorrectionLogRepository |
| Description and Purpose | Manages all write and read operations on the CorrectionLog table; exposes methods for creating correction records and retrieving correction history by session or sample |
| Component Type / Format | Repository class / data access object |

* Object-Oriented Components

  * Class Diagram

1. **Diagram 1: Input and Validation**

**![][image75]**

2. **Diagram 2: Submission Flow and On-Device Persistence** 

**![][image76]**

3. **Diagram 3: Backend Processing**

**![][image77]**

The three diagrams follow the administrator retrieval transaction in order: the administrator authenticates through AdministratorLoginScreen, which gates all subsequent access behind AdminAuthenticationHandler and issues an AdminSession token that scopes every downstream request → the authenticated administrator browses the UploadedSessionsList filtered by FilterControlsPanel parameters, selects a session to expand in SessionReportDetailPanel, and triggers file delivery through DownloadPDFButton or DownloadCSVButton, with all list and detail state driven by UploadedSessionSummary and SessionReportDetail objects → the backend serves list queries through UploadedSessionQueryHandler applying the combined filter contract, and serves file downloads through ReportDeliveryService which streams the requested file from server storage and fires RetrievalLogger to write a timestamped retrieval record for every download event. AdminSession, SessionReportQueryParams, and ReportDeliveryRequest bridge all three diagrams as the shared contracts carrying authentication context and filter intent from the frontend through backend query and file delivery.
